messages:
jordan: hey team — new hire hit a weird quickstart issue on Windows (WSL2). curl to https://api.redwood.com/v1/first-call returns 403 initially, then 200 after retrying manually. Workspace UI shows 'Billing required' even though org billing is active. rehired user is blocked from first successful call.

jordan: curl output: ```
$ curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_KEY' https://api.redwood.com/v1/models
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2026 18:02:35 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "org_billing_needed",
  "message": "This workspace requires billing to make requests."
}
```

lee: is the key definitely from the right workspace? sometimes people paste sandbox keys. can you paste the workspace id (not the key) and the exact env var command they used?

jordan: workspace id is org_01G7X... (redacted). They set env like `setx REDWOOD_API_KEY \"sk_...\"` in cmd.exe, then used curl inside WSL.

morgan: that pattern screams proxy/wsl header rewrite. corp proxies on Windows can strip/modify Authorization header when crossing the host-proxy boundary. if they set the key in Windows env and then call from WSL, the header might not be forwarded. does the same curl from native Windows (PowerShell) behave differently?

jordan: good call — ran from PowerShell, first try 200. from WSL it was 403.

sam: also check for the deploy-bot billing alert in the org logs — looks like a webhook fired earlier. deploy-bot: "billing-webhook: workspace org_01G7X flagged trial-expiry ping (sent to billing-service)"

morgan: try explicitly exporting the key in the WSL session rather than relying on Windows env passthrough: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_...` then `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/models`

jordan: tried that and it worked — immediate 200. so the root cause is env propagation + proxy header stripping between WSL and host.

lee: thanks — two follow-ups: 1) doc update for quickstart Windows/WSL note, 2) suggest adding a diagnostic hint in SDK errors when we see org_billing_needed + incoming agent appears to be via WSL/proxy? maybe detect missing Authorization header at edge and return a slightly more helpful message (e.g., hint about proxies/WSL).

sam: agree on docs. on the edge side we only see a missing/invalid auth — adding heuristics might be noisy. instead, add a short troubleshooting FAQ entry and a CLI check `redwood doctor` that prints common env/proxy pitfalls.

jordan: filed a tiny PR updating the quickstart Windows section and added a troubleshooting snippet: ```
# in WSL
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_xxx
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
```

jordan: resolved for the user — first successful call confirmed :tada: They also removed the company proxy for that host via `NO_PROXY=api.redwood.com` and it stopped rewriting the header.

morgan: assigning to docs to add a short note and to devex to consider a `redwood doctor` ticket. filing internal ticket DEVEX-482 for doctor + FAQ.

lee: can we also add a one-liner in onboarding checklist for new hires using Windows: "if using WSL, export key inside WSL or set NO_PROXY for api.redwood.com"

jordan: done in onboarding checklist. thanks all. :thumbsup:
